# dsh-trigger-hub

> Give DeepSeek Harness agents something to react to: cron/interval schedules,
> authenticated webho

oks, file watchers and deterministic procedures — with one
> ledger, one console and one concurrency

le watchers and deterministic procedures — with one
> ledger, one console and one concurrency limit.

`dsh-trigger-hub` is a small, dependency-free DSH bundle. It is an event source,
not a workflow engi

ne: it turns one external event into one agent run and records
what happened. The agent itself decid
es what the run means.
## Why

DSH sessions are reactive: a person opens a chat, or another plugin creates a
session and prompts it

. Recurring jobs, CI notifications and file changes usually
end up as bespoke glue scripts around th

ring jobs, CI notifications and file changes usually
end up as bespoke glue scripts around the host.
This bundle keeps that glue in one place:

- **Schedule**: `cron: "0 9 * * *"` or `every: 6h`.
- **Webhook**: `POST /dsh-trigger-hub/hook/<id>`

with a per-source token.
- **Watch**: `fs.watch` on a path, debounced.
- **Procedure**: run one she

ll command without a model call; a failure can
escalate to an agent session or an HTTP endpoint.
- *

*Sink**: create/resume a DSH session and prompt it, or POST the event to an
HTTP endpoint (for examp

le a super-agent router).
- **Policy**: enable/pause, duplicate suppression, concurrency limit, quie

t hours.
- **Ledger**: last 200 runs, counters and a read-only console page.

## Configuration
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Source fields
| Field | Applies to | Meaning |

| `id` | all | Stable id used in routes, the ledger and the console. Required |
| `kind` | all | `sc

hedule`, `webhook`, `watch` or `procedure` |
| `enabled` | all | `false` disables the source without

removing it |
| `cron` / `every` | schedule | Five-field cron or an interval (`30s`, `5m`, `6h`, `2

d`); exactly one |
| `token` / `tokenEnv` | webhook | Shared token; `tokenEnv` reads it from the env

ironment at request time |
| `path` | watch | File or directory to watch |
| `debounceMs` | watch |

Coalescing window, default `1500` |
| `prompt` | all | Text for the session sink; `{{payload}}` is r

eplaced with the event JSON |
| `quietHours` | all | `{from: "22:00", to: "07:00"}` suppresses fires

, wrapping midnight |
| `sink` | all | `{kind: "session", cwd?, preset?, prompt?}` (default for non-

procedures) or `{kind: "http", url, method?, headers?}` |
| `command` | procedure | Shell command to

run with `/bin/bash -lc`; required |
| `timeoutMs` | procedure | Kill the command after this long,

default `600000` |
| `expectExitCode` | procedure | Exit code treated as success, default `0` |
| `c

aptureChars` | procedure | Output tail kept in the run record, default `4000` |
| `onFailure` | proc

edure | Sink to fire when the command fails or times out |
| `onSuccess` | procedure | Optional sink
to fire on success (same shape as `sink`) |

A `schedule` source fires its sink and reschedules itself. A `watch` source
debounces filesystem eve

nts. A `webhook` source only fires when called with the
right token.
### Procedures

A procedure is the deterministic fast path: no model call, just one command and
an exit-code verdict

. It can be fired manually, or scheduled with the same
`cron` / `every` fields as a schedule source.

On failure the optional
`onFailure` sink receives a payload containing `procedure.output` and runs

an
agent session (or an HTTP post), so judgment is spent only when something went
wrong.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The run record keeps the exit code, duration and a bounded output tail. A
procedure runs with the ho

st user's permissions; treat the command as trusted
configuration, not as untrusted input.
### Session sink

The hub creates a Session named `trigger-hub-<source>-<runId>` in the configured
`cwd`, using the op

tional agent preset, then queues the prompt. If a Session with
that id already exists it is resumed

and prompted instead. The hub never runs
tools itself; the agent session owns the work.
### HTTP sink

The hub POSTs `{source, runId, payload}` as JSON to the configured URL. Any
non-2xx response marks t

he run failed. This is the integration point for an
external router or task queue.
## HTTP surface
| Method | Path | Auth | Meaning |
| POST | `/dsh-trigger-hub/hook/<source-id>` | `x-trigger-token` header or `?token=` | Fire a webhoo

k source |
| POST | `/dsh-trigger-hub/run/<source-id>` | loopback only | Fire any source manually |

| GET | `/dsh-trigger-hub/state` | loopback or same origin | Ledger snapshot (JSON) |
| GET | `/dsh-

trigger-hub/health` | loopback or same origin | Health (JSON) |
| GET | `/dsh-trigger-hub/panel` | l
oopback or same origin | Console page |

Webhook bodies must be JSON and are limited to 64 KiB. A repeated delivery with
the same `id`/`deliv

ery`/`key` inside `dedupeWindowMs` is suppressed and counted
as `deduped`, without calling the sink.
## Security

- Webhook sources require a token; a missing token, an empty token, or a source
without `token`/`tok

enEnv` is rejected.
- Use `tokenEnv` so the token lives in the environment, not in a profile file.
-

The console and state routes are available only to loopback clients or
same-origin requests.
- The

hub does not start a public listener of its own: it uses the DSH web
server. If the host is exposed

beyond loopback, put it behind your normal
authentication and TLS.
- The ledger stores prompts, even

t payloads and error strings. Do not send
secrets in webhook payloads.
